incidents.what: Re-tokenized en_c4 single-process for a t31 rehearsal while 44 held a warm cache and ran 8 encoders. My job starved theirs and died in the 120s startup gate mid-tokenize.
incidents.evidence: runs/t31_rehearsal.log, one tokenize line and no step lines; facts/efficiency.json#eff.cache_load_gates_startup, contended 0.07 GiB/s against 0.39 effective
incidents.root_cause: I read idle cards as an idle pod. The contended resource was CPU and page cache, which nvidia-smi does not report.
incidents.landed_or_proposed: Landed: launch_30b.sh names no gate and harness launch derives it from mix cache bytes. Proposed: --dry refuses when a domain cache is cold.
incidents.differently: Enumerate every resource a job consumes and check each one. Ask the owner of a cache before rebuilding it.

incidents.what: Ran harness task done for t01 and t02 on the pod. The repo copy of runs/tasks.jsonl is canonical and the pod copy is push-only, so both closes were lost.
incidents.evidence: runs/tasks.jsonl, both tasks closed in the repo only after fb's correction; scripts/pod_push.sh pushes tasks.jsonl and never reads it back
incidents.root_cause: I assumed a file present on both sides syncs both ways. The sync is one-way and nothing refuses the write on the read-only side.
incidents.landed_or_proposed: Proposed: harness task refuses to run on the pod, the same guard shape as its worktree check at scripts/harness.py:2491.
incidents.differently: Establish which copy of a shared state file is canonical before writing to it.

incidents.what: Reported 1.5-1.6 GiB/s as the measured cache read rate and sized the stage-1 gate from it. That rate is one reader on an idle disk. Seven ranks share a page cache and get 0.39 GiB/s. A gate derived from 1.5 is 192s, below the 600s floor, so it reads as correct and does nothing. My 1800s was safe by accident.
incidents.caused_or_missed: caused, caught by de before it shipped
incidents.evidence: facts/efficiency.json#eff.cache_load_gates_startup separates 0.39 per-rank startup, 1.55 single-stream warm, 1.30 raw dd, 0.07 contended; commit ad89736
incidents.root_cause: I measured one regime and reported it as the property. Single-stream and 7-rank-concurrent differ by 4.0x.
incidents.landed_or_proposed: Landed: the fact names all four rates and which one sizes the gate. harness launch owns the derivation through _CACHE_READ_GIBPS. Two docstrings that still said 1.5 GiB/s now cite the constant.
incidents.differently: State the regime beside every rate. Measure a number under the conditions that will consume it.

incidents.what: Wrote a fallback pod-sync script whose delete logic would have removed live train.py and harness.py, from a HEAD~1 baseline and from a pod-manifest baseline.
incidents.caused_or_missed: caused, caught by my own dry run before it ran
incidents.root_cause: I read absent from the baseline as should be deleted. It also means the baseline is incomplete, and it was.
incidents.landed_or_proposed: Landed by deletion: dropped the script once pod_push.sh --all existed.
incidents.differently: Dry-run a destructive path against the real tree before writing it. Prefer waiting for a peer's tool over shipping a parallel one.

class_removed: A measurement or a file treated as regime-independent. Three of the four incidents have this shape: a rate measured single-stream and used to size a 7-rank load, a file that syncs one way and was written to on the read side, a baseline read as complete when it was partial. Landed: the startup gate is derived from mix cache bytes instead of a carried number. Next: --dry refuses a launch whose caches are cold.
note: Written during pretrain_15b_s1 at step 630, loss 2.408, 77K tok/s/GPU, MFU 32%. No change to the launch path until step 1000, per fb.

incidents.what: Reported code_500 = 2.20% for the t39 dry run to the controller. The measurement is 0.0% (0/500). I read the number off readout_30b.py's docstring, which carries a v2 example, instead of the record I had just written.
incidents.evidence: runs/score_matrix.jsonl ckpt_p324.pt profile=milestone: {'code_500': 0.0, '_wall_s': 591.2}; runs/readout_ckpt_p324.txt; correction in runs/tasks.jsonl t39
incidents.root_cause: I quoted a number from prose next to the data instead of from the data. The wrong value was higher than the true one, so it read as a plausible result and nothing in the pipeline disagreed with it.
incidents.landed_or_proposed: Landed: corrected to fb and in t39's evidence. Proposed: harness milestone already writes the verdict to runs/readout_<ckpt>.txt -- report from that file, never from memory of a run.
incidents.differently: Quote measurements only from the artifact that produced them, with its path in the same sentence.

incidents.what: My one-off .part adoption split one document into four invalid JSON fragments in code_rp1t_197.jsonl. 44's independent count hit them and the launch-path corpus looked corrupt.
incidents.evidence: data/corpus/code_rp1t/code_rp1t_197.jsonl lines 2780-2783; repaired by /tmp/fix197.py; stamp fingerprint 7f17d205b3d5acb7 -> d8b9b18ba080f487
incidents.root_cause: str.splitlines() breaks on U+2028/U+2029/U+0085; json.dumps leaves those raw inside a string. I used splitlines() to drop a truncated final line.
incidents.landed_or_proposed: Landed: rejoin, all 235 shards verified with strict json.loads, malformed_lines: 0 recorded in the stamp; tilerl's tokenize read all 3,747,157 docs clean, independent of my sweep.
incidents.differently: Split JSONL on \n only. Never splitlines() on a file whose lines are JSON.

incidents.what: Wrote the auto-resume selftest so it called exp.py without a root override. It appended four real rows named 'arts' to runs/experiments.jsonl, two sharing an identity, which then failed the sync guard.
incidents.evidence: four rows name=arts, started 2026-08-31 20:32-20:33, removed in 89ab3bb; _verify_merge duplicate-identity error
incidents.root_cause: exp.py takes no ambient root override by design (the ledger gets no env var). A test that cannot redirect a writer writes to the real thing.
incidents.landed_or_proposed: Landed: _supervise and _close_row take an explicit root; the selftest passes a temp dir and suppresses the monitor.
incidents.differently: Before writing a test for code that writes a ledger, check how the test redirects the write. If it cannot, that is the first thing to fix.

incidents.what: Nearly shipped the startup-gate derivation with a 1.5 GiB/s constant taken from tilerl's warm single-stream measurement. It derives 198 s for a startup that took 386 s, below the 600 s floor, so every mix would have fallen back to the floor and the derivation would have done nothing while looking correct.
incidents.evidence: facts/efficiency.json#eff.cache_load_gates_startup, three separate rates; _selftest_gate_timeout asserts 149 GiB -> > 386 s
incidents.root_cause: A rate measured in one regime (one reader, idle disk) used to predict another (7 ranks sharing a page cache). Same class as counting tokens without the <eos> the encoder appends.
incidents.landed_or_proposed: Landed: _CACHE_READ_GIBPS = 0.39, derived as 149 GiB / 386 s, with the derivation in the constant's comment; selftest asserts against the real startup, not against the formula.
incidents.differently: Assert a derived constant against the outcome it must predict, not against its own arithmetic.

incidents.what: Implemented fb's manual-count ratchet as _MANUAL_BASELINE = len(_MANUAL_RULES). It moves with the set it pins, so it could never fire.
incidents.evidence: d94fce6; verified check_agents_rules_covered returns FAIL when a rule is added and the literal stays 20
incidents.root_cause: A ratchet computed from the thing it ratchets is not a ratchet. Two mappings in the same table also claimed more than their checks assert (pinned_ids for the tokenizer freeze, score_input_fresh for vocabulary identity); both demoted, checked count 15 -> 14.
incidents.landed_or_proposed: Landed: literal baseline, honest mappings, and the manual column states what each check cannot see.
incidents.differently: A guard's baseline is a literal that a commit must change. Verify a new guard fires before believing it.

class_removed: Numbers that do not carry their configuration. Three of tonight's five incidents are one shape: a value correct in one context reused in another -- tokens without <eos> (0.35% low), a read rate from one reader applied to seven, a docstring example quoted as a measurement. scripts/count_tokens.py makes the token count one definition; _CACHE_READ_GIBPS carries its derivation; the gate selftest asserts against the measured startup. The general fix is in the checks, not in care.
note: The deletion pass nearly removed 23 live math generators: vet_programs.py globs math_programs_l*_ext*.py at runtime, so a name-scan sees them as unreferenced. reachability.py reports 0 unreachable partly because doc citations count as edges. Neither is a deletion oracle for a repo with a runtime loader.
